title: Challenge: SSH remote port forward
intro: Your web app runs on your laptop at localhost:3000, but the laptop is behind NAT, nobody outside can reach it. You do have SSH access to a public box, bastion.example.com. Expose your app through it with a remote port forward.

steps.instruction: Open a remote forward so bastion.example.com:8080 points back to your laptop's localhost:3000, with no remote shell.
steps.success: Remote forward established: bastion.example.com:8080 -> your laptop's localhost:3000.
steps.fail: Use ssh -R REMOTE_PORT:HOST:PORT to user@bastion.example.com. Add -N for no remote shell.

steps.instruction: On the bastion, verify it reaches your app: run a client against its local port 8080.
steps.success:
It works, served from your laptop

(the request tunneled back to localhost:3000)
steps.fail: Run a client (e.g. curl) against localhost:8080 on the bastion.

done: Solved! `ssh -R` exposed a service behind NAT through a public box. (For the bastion to listen on all interfaces, it needs GatewayPorts yes.)
